title: A {Cr2Dy4} compressed octahedron: the first sulfate-based single-molecule magnet

synthesis.procedure: Main text: hydrothermal reaction of Dy(NO3)3·6H2O, Cr(NO3)3·9H2O, Na2SO4 and piperazine in a 2:1:3:4 molar ratio; experimental details are given in the ESI. SI: all analytical-grade reagents were used as received. A mixture of Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.228 g, 0.50 mmol), Cr(NO3)3·9H2O (0.100 g, 0.25 mmol), Na2SO4 (0.106 g, 0.75 mmol), piperazine (0.086 g, 1.0 mmol) and water (10 mL) was stirred at room temperature for 30 min, transferred to a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel vessel, and heated at 170 °C for 3 days under autogenous pressure. After slow cooling to room temperature, cube-shaped red crystals of 1 were obtained. Yield 0.136 g (62% based on Dy(NO3)3). Elemental analysis found C 2.86, H 2.23, N 1.45%; C4H40N2O42S6Cr2Dy4 requires C 2.77, H 2.32, N 1.61%. IR (KBr) νmax/cm−1: 3384, 1654, 1608, 1436, 1234, 1091, 1051, 987, 644, 597 and 554.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: hydrothermal reaction in a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel vessel under autogenous pressure
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling to room temperature afforded cube-shaped red crystals.

properties.summary: Compound 1 is a sulfate-based single-molecule magnet. DC susceptibility indicates dominant antiferromagnetic interactions arranged ferrimagnetically, with thermal depopulation of Dy(III) Stark levels and a large uncompensated spin ground state. Magnetization does not saturate and M vs H/T curves do not superimpose, consistent with anisotropy and/or low-lying excited states. Zero-field ac susceptibility is strongly frequency dependent (φ = 0.19), and the relaxation follows an Arrhenius law. A large Cole–Cole α at 3.0 K indicates a broad distribution and likely multiple relaxation processes associated with two crystallographically distinct Dy(III) sites.

measurements.name: magnetization
measurements.conditions: 2.0 K, 7 T; no saturation (expected 46 μB for four non-interacting Dy(III) and two Cr(III))

measurements.name: φ
measurements.conditions: φ = (ΔTp/Tp)/Δ(log f) from frequency-dependent χ′ peaks; zero dc field, superparamagnetic range

measurements.name: Ueff/kB
measurements.conditions: Arrhenius fit of temperature-dependent relaxation times from ac peak temperatures, zero dc field
